```{r data}
## ---------------------------
##' [IPEDS/Carnegie Classification Data]
## ---------------------------

# load IPEDS data and merge with the Carnegie Classification

ipeds24 <- read_csv("../data/sources/hd2024.csv")
ipeds_cost <- read_csv("../data/sources/cost1_2024.csv")
#ipeds_schoolsize <- read_csv("../data/sources/ef2024a.csv") #enrollment Fall 2024
carnegie <- read_excel("../data/sources/2025-Public-Data-File.xlsx", sheet = 2)
ic2024 <- read_csv("../data/sources/ic2024.csv")
sfa <- read_csv("../data/sources/sfa2324.csv")
adm <- read_csv("../data/sources/adm2024.csv")
enroll <- read_csv("../data/sources/effy2024.csv") %>%
  filter(EFFYALEV == 3) %>%  #degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates
  select(UNITID, EFFYALEV, EFYTOTLT, EFYAIANT, EFYBKAAT, EFYNHPIT, EFYWHITT, EFYHISPT, EFYASIAT, EFYNRALT) 


ipeds_dist <- read_csv("../data/sources/effy2024_dist.csv") |> 
  filter(EFFYDLEV == 2) |>    #undergrad total
  select(UNITID, EFFYDLEV, EFYDETOT, EFYDEEXC)


ipeds_learner<- read_csv("../data/sources/ef2023b.csv") |> 
  filter(LSTUDY == 2, , EFBAGE %in% c(1, 7)) |>   #undergrad total / all age categories total, age 25 and over total
  select(UNITID, EFBAGE, EFAGE06, EFAGE09) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = EFBAGE, 
              values_from = c(EFAGE06, EFAGE09))


carnegie <- carnegie |> 
  select(unitid, hsi)

ipeds_exp <- read_csv("../data/sources/drvf2024.csv")  |>
  select(UNITID, F1INSTFT, F2INSTFT, F3INSTFT, F1RSRCFT, F2RSRCFT, F3RSRCFT)

ipeds_programs <- read_csv("../data/sources/c2024dep.csv") |> 
  filter(CIPCODE == 99) |> 
  select(UNITID, PTOTAL, PTOTALDE) 

```


```{r Merge source data}

# merge files
sources <- ipeds24 %>% 
  left_join(carnegie, by = c("UNITID" = "unitid")) %>% 
  left_join(ipeds_cost, by = "UNITID") |> 
  #left_join(ipeds_schoolsize, by = "UNITID") %>%
  left_join(ic2024, by = "UNITID" ) %>%
  left_join(sfa, by = "UNITID") %>%
  left_join(adm, by = "UNITID") %>%
  left_join(enroll, by = "UNITID") |> 
  left_join(ipeds_dist, by = "UNITID") |> 
  left_join(ipeds_learner, by = "UNITID") |> 
  left_join(ipeds_exp, by = "UNITID") |> 
  left_join(ipeds_programs, by = "UNITID")



# select variables and create a dataset for analysis
x <- sources |>
    rename_all(tolower)

# assign to "data"
sources <- x


```


```{r Create Sample}

x <- sources %>% 
  filter(fips <= 56) |>                                            # Keep only 50 states and DC                                         (-138)
  filter(cbsa != -2) |>                                            # Remove colleges not located in CBSAs                               (-267)
  filter(ugoffer == 1) |>                                          # Offers undergraduate programs                                      (-281)
  filter(pseflag == 1) |>                                          # Active postsecondary institution                                   (-76)
  filter(!is.na(iclevel) & iclevel != 3 & iclevel != -3) |>        # 3: less than 2 years  or unknown                                   (-1,573)
  filter(instcat >= 2 & instcat <= 4) |>                           # 1: degree-granting, graduate with no undergraduate degrees         (-341)
                                                                   # 5-6: non-degree-granting
  filter(distnced != 1) |>                                         # 1: completely distanced learning                                   (-62)
  filter(opeflag == 1 | opeflag == 2) |>                           # Title IV eligible institutions                                     (-54)
  filter(carnegieapm != 12) |>                                     # Remove theology colleges
  filter(control != 3)

 


initial_sample <- x  # (2,524 institutions)

```


```{r Data cleaning}


x <- initial_sample |> 
  mutate(
         public = case_when(
            control == 2 ~ 0,                             # 0: private
            control == 1 ~ 1,                             # 1: public 
            # control == 3 ~ 2,                             # 2: for-profit
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),   
         
         twoyear = case_when(
            iclevel == 1 ~ 0,                             # 0: 4 or more
            iclevel == 2 ~ 1,                             # 1: at least 2 & less than 4
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),     
         
                           
         inst_type = case_when(                 
           sector == 4 ~ 0,                      # 0: Public 2-year 
           sector == 5 ~ 1,                      # 1: Private 2-year 
           sector == 1 ~ 2,                      # 2: Public 4year or above
           sector == 2 ~ 3,                      # 3: Private 4-year                      
          
           TRUE ~ NA_real_
         ),
         
         msi = case_when(                                 # 0: non of them
            hbcu == 1   ~ 1,                              # 1: HBCU
            hsi == 1    ~ 2,                              # 2: HSI
            tribal == 1 ~ 3,                              # 3: TCU
            TRUE        ~ 0),
         
         # msi = case_when(
         #   hbcu == 1 | hsi == 1 | tribal == 1 ~ 1, 
         #   TRUE ~ 0),
         
         rurality = case_when(
            locale %in% c(31,32,33,41,42,43) ~ 0,         # 0: Town + Rural
            locale %in% c(21,22,23) ~ 1,                  # 1: Suburb
            locale %in% c(11,12,13) ~ 2,                  # 2: City
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),        
         
         rurality = factor(rurality,
                           levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                           labels = c("Town/Rural", "Suburb", "City")),

         # size = case_when(
         #   # !is.na(instsize), instsize - 1, NA_real_),
         #   
         #   instsize %in% c(1, 2)        ~ 0,                       # 0: < 3,999
         #   # instsize == 2              ~ 1,
         #   instsize == 3               ~ 1,                       # 1: 4,000 - 19,999
         #   instsize %in% c(4,5)        ~ 2,                       # 2: >=20,000
         #   TRUE ~ NA_real_),
         
         

         # tuitionnn = ntile(tuition1, 3),  1,               # 0~3: quartiles
         # tuitionnn = if_else(is.na(tuition1), 0, tuitionnn),
         # #chg1ay1

#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_cost$TUITION1))  [1] 2,368 (= about 40% of the sample)

         housing = case_when(
           room == 2 ~ 0,                                 # 0: no housing
           room == 1 ~ 1,                                 # 1: offer housing
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),    

         religious = ifelse(relaffil == -2, 0, 1),        # 0: no religious
                                                          # 1: any religious
         
         online = case_when(
            is.na(efydetot) ~ NA_real_,
            #is.na(efydeexc) & xefdeexc == "A" ~ 0,         # "A": not applicable
            is.na(efydeexc) ~ NA_real_,                    # other missing cases
            TRUE ~ efydeexc / efydetot),



        online_progs = ptotalde/ptotal,                   #Proportion of programs that can be completed entirely online


#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_dist$EFDETOT))  [1] 0

        evening = case_when(
          slo7 == 0 ~ 0,                                  # 0: no weekend/evening courses
          slo7 == 1 ~ 1,                                  # 1: allows classes only on weekends or only in evenings
          TRUE ~ NA_real_),

#check missing values: sum(is.na(ic2024$SLO7))  [1] 0
        

        adult = case_when(
            is.na(efage09_7) ~ NA_real_,
            is.na(efage09_1) ~ NA_real_,
            TRUE ~ efage09_7 / efage09_1),


#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_learner$EFAGE09_1))  [1] 0
#check missing values: sum(is.na(ipeds_learner$EFAGE09_7))  [1] 9



         sports = case_when(
           athassoc == 2 ~ 0,                             # 0: not a member
           athassoc == 1 ~ 1,                             # 1: member of National Athletic Association
           TRUE ~NA_real_),

         loan = case_when(
           is.na(loan_a) ~ NA_real_,
           loan_a <= quantile(loan_a, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 0,     # 0: lowest
           loan_a <= quantile(loan_a, 0.50, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1,     # 1: low 
           loan_a <= quantile(loan_a, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) ~ 2,     # 2: high
           TRUE ~ 3),                                              # 3: highest
 
# Q. Since MLCA requires variables starting at 0, is it appropriate to divide loan amount into quartiles (0–3)?

         asc = case_when(
           carnegiesaec == 2 ~ 0,                         # 0: Higher Access, Lower Earnings 
           carnegiesaec == 4 ~ 1,                         # 1: Higher Access, Medium Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 6 ~ 2,                         # 2: Higher Access, Higher Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 1 ~ 3,                         # 3: Lower Access, Lower Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 3 ~ 4,                         # 4: Lower Access, Medium Earnings
           carnegiesaec == 5 ~ 5,                         # 5: Lower Access, Higher Earnings
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),

         awardlev = case_when(
           carnegiealf %in% c(1, 2) ~ 0,                    # 0: associates 
           carnegiealf == 3 ~ 1,                            # 1: baccalaureate
           carnegiealf == 4 ~ 2,                            # 2: masters
           carnegiealf == 5 ~ 3,                            # 3: doctoral

           carnegiealf == -2 & (hloffer == 3 | hloffer == 4) ~ 0,
           hloffer == 5 & instcat == 2 ~ 1,
           
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),
         #Check: x %>% filter(is.na(awardlev)) %>% View()

         special_focus = case_when(
            carnegieapm <= 1                             ~ 0,   # 0: Not special focus
            carnegieapm == 2                             ~ 1,   # 2: Professions focused
            carnegieapm == 3                             ~ 2,  # 3: Applied and career studies
            carnegieapm %in% c(4,5)                      ~ 3,  # 4: Arts and sciences
            carnegieapm == 6                             ~ 4,  # 5: Business
            carnegieapm %in% c(8,9,10)                   ~ 5,  # 6: Medical sciences/health
            carnegieapm == 11                            ~ 6,  # 7: STEM

            TRUE ~ NA_real_), 

            #carnegieapm == 1                           ~ 1,  # 1: Mixed
            # carnegieapm == 3                           ~ 3,  # 3: Applied and career studies
            # carnegieapm %in% c(4,5)                    ~ 4,  # 4: Arts and sciences
            # carnegieapm == 6                           ~ 5,  # 5: Business
            # carnegieapm %in% c(8,9,10)                 ~ 6,  # 6: Medical sciences/health
            # carnegieapm == 11                          ~ 7,  # 7: STEM
            # carnegieapm == 12                          ~ 3,  # 8: Theology
                                    
        
        research = case_when( 
            carnegiersch == -2 ~ 0,                   #0: No research designation
            carnegiersch == 3 ~ 1,                    #1: 4-year, Research Colleges and Universities
            carnegiersch == 2 ~ 2,                   #2: High Spending
            carnegiersch == 1 ~ 3,                   #3: Very High Spending
            TRUE ~ NA_real_),    


         
         cbsa = as.character(cbsa),

         cbsatype = case_when(
           cbsatype == 2 ~ 0,   # Micropolitan
           cbsatype == 1 ~ 1,   # Metropolitan
           TRUE ~ NA_real_),


        # # pell = ntile(upgrntp, 4) - 1,                         # 0~3: quartiles
        # pell = case_when(
        #   upgrntp < 10 ~ 0,
        #   upgrntp >= 10 & upgrntp < 25 ~ 1,
        #   upgrntp >= 25 ~ 2,
        #   TRUE ~ NA_real_
        # ),
        
        instruction_exp_fte = coalesce(f1instft, f2instft, f3instft),
        # instruction_exp = ntile(instruction_exp_fte, 4) - 1,  # 0-2: tertiles
        # instruction_exp = case_when(
        #   instruction_exp_fte < 5000                                     ~ 0,
        #   instruction_exp_fte >= 5000 & instruction_exp_fte < 10000      ~ 1,
        #   instruction_exp_fte >= 10000 & instruction_exp_fte < 50000     ~ 2, 
        #   instruction_exp_fte >= 50000                                   ~ 3,
        #   TRUE ~ NA_real_
        # ),

        research_exp_fte = coalesce(f1rsrcft, f2rsrcft, f3rsrcft),
        # research_exp = case_when(
        #   research_exp_fte == 0                                          ~ 0,
        #   research_exp_fte > 0 & research_exp_fte < 1000                 ~ 1,
        #   research_exp_fte >= 1000 & research_exp_fte < 10000            ~ 2,
        #   research_exp_fte >=10000                                       ~ 3,
        #   TRUE ~ NA_real_
        # ),

        # research_exp = ntile(research_exp_fte, 4) - 1,

        international_n = efynralt, 
  
        # num_degrees = ntile(ptotal, 4) - 1,
        
        system = if_else(f1systyp == 1, 1, 0)
  
       )




cleaned_data <- x |>
  group_by(cbsa) %>% 
  mutate(inst_num = n_distinct(unitid),
         inst_num = as.numeric(inst_num)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(admrate = admssn/applcn) %>% 
  mutate(selectivity = if_else(openadmp == 1, 1, admrate)) |>
  mutate(
    # selectivity = case_when(
    #      openadmp == 1 ~ 0,
    #      admrate == 1 ~ 0,                        #0: open 
    #      admrate >= 0.75 & admrate < 1 ~ 1,       #1: less selective
    #      admrate >= 0.40 & admrate < 0.75 ~ 2,    #2: selective
    #      admrate < 0.40 ~ 3,                      #3: more selective
    #      TRUE ~ NA_real_),
         
         i_perc_black = efybkaat/efytotlt,              #Percent of degree-seeking undergrads by race/ethnicity
         i_perc_white = efywhitt/efytotlt,
         i_perc_hisp = efyhispt/efytotlt,
         i_perc_nhpi = (efyaiant + efynhpit)/efytotlt,
         i_perc_asian = efyasiat/efytotlt,

         nonwhite = 1 - i_perc_white
         ) %>% 
           
  rename(
        region = obereg,
         size = instsize,
         tuitionnn = tuition1,
         pell = upgrntp,
         num_degrees = ptotal
         ) %>% 
  
  mutate(
         pell = pell/100,
         cbsa = as.character(cbsa),
         unitid = as.character(unitid),
         region = as.factor(region),
         cbsatype = as.factor(cbsatype),
         public = as.factor(public),
         twoyear = as.factor(twoyear),
         inst_type = as.factor(inst_type),
         awardlev = as.factor(awardlev),
         system = as.factor(system),
         size = as.factor(size),
         msi = as.factor(msi),
         religious = as.factor(religious),
         special_focus = as.factor(special_focus),
         housing = as.factor(housing),
         evening = as.factor(evening),
         ) |> 
  # filter(online < .9) |>                                                        # Remove colleges with 90% or more students enrolled exclusively online

  select(
    unitid, instnm, stabbr, cbsa, cbsatype, region,
    public, twoyear, inst_type, awardlev, system,
    msi, religious, special_focus, size, selectivity,
    housing, rurality, online_progs, evening, adult, pell, nonwhite,
    instruction_exp_fte, research_exp_fte, tuitionnn,
     num_degrees, international_n)
```

```{r student pop data}

pop_data <- read_csv("../data/sources/effy2024.csv") %>% 
  filter(EFFYLEV == 2 | EFFYLEV == 4) %>% 
  select(UNITID, EFFYALEV, EFYTOTLT) %>% 
  mutate(EFFYALEV = if_else(EFFYALEV == 2, "undergrad", "grad")) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "UNITID",
              names_from = EFFYALEV, 
              values_from = EFYTOTLT) %>% 
  mutate(i_total_pop = rowSums(pick(undergrad, grad), na.rm = TRUE),
         per_undergrad = undergrad/i_total_pop,
         per_grad = grad/i_total_pop,
         unitid = as.character(UNITID)) |> 
  select(-UNITID)

data <- cleaned_data |>
  left_join(pop_data, by = "unitid")

```




```{r Check bivariate associations between variables}

# install.packages("rstatix")
 library(rstatix)


test <- data %>% 
  select(public, twoyear, inst_type, awardlev, system,
    msi, religious, special_focus, size,
    housing, rurality, evening) 

test[] <- lapply(test, as.factor) 

variable_pairs <- expand.grid(Var1 = names(test), Var2 = names(test), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(Var1 < Var2)

# Calculate Cramér's V
results_matrix <- variable_pairs %>%
  mutate(Cramers_V = map2_dbl(Var1, Var2, ~ cramer_v(test[[.x]], test[[.y]]))) |> 
  arrange(Var1, Cramers_V)

print(results_matrix)

#Variables to not use in the analysis:
  # twoyear
  # public
  # housing
  # religious
  # size
  

#Test correlations
corr_test <- data |> 
  select(selectivity, online_progs, adult, pell, nonwhite,instruction_exp_fte, research_exp_fte, tuitionnn,
     num_degrees, international_n, i_total_pop) |> 
  cor(, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

print(corr_test)

#Variables to not use in the analysis:
 # research_exp_fte
 # selectivity


```

```{r census/ACS data}
                  year = 2024,
                  variables = c("B01003_001E", # Total population
                                "B19013_001E", # Median Household Income in the Past 12 Months
                                "DP03_0119PE", # % families below poverty line
                                "DP03_0005PE", # % unemployed over 16 years old
                                "DP02_0068PE", # % bach or higher
                                "B03002_003E", # total white (alone, not hispanic)
                                "B03002_004E", # total black (alone, not hispanic)
                                "B03002_012E", # total hispanic
                                "B03002_006E", # total asian (alone, not hispanic)
                                "B03002_001E"  # total by ethnicity
                  ),
                  output = "wide") %>% 
  left_join(land_area)


census <- census |>
  mutate(perc_white = B03002_003E/B03002_001E*100,
         perc_black = B03002_004E/B03002_001E*100,
         perc_hisp = B03002_012E/B03002_001E*100,
         perc_asian = B03002_006E/B03002_001E*100,
         tot_pop = B01003_001E/100000,
         pop_density = B01003_001E/(ALAND/2589988.10)) |> #population per sq mile

  select(tot_pop, pop_density, perc_ba,
         med_income, perc_pov, perc_unemployed,
         perc_white, perc_black, perc_hisp, perc_asian,
         GEOID) |> 
  mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID))
```

Indicators for classifying postsecondary institutions are based on framework for insitutional diversity in: 
# Harris, M.S. An Empirical Typology of the Institutional Diversity of U.S. Colleges and Universities. Innov High Educ 45, 183–199 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10755-019-09494-6

 Systemic- structural and governance characteristics
  inst_type, system
  
  Programmatic- degree level and academic disciplinary offerings
    awardlev, special_focus, num_degrees
 
 Procedural- how programs are offered and implemented
    online_progs, evening, instructional_exp_fte, tuitionnn
 
 Constituential- "student demographics, background, preparation, and abilities" (Harris, 2020 p.187)
  msi, adult, pell, nonwhite, per_undergrad, i_total_pop, selectivity
 
 
STEP 1: 
Conduct a principal component factor analysis on variables that reflect institutional characteristics. The goal is to condense a wide set of correlated variables into a smaller set of orthogonal components that capture the maximum variance within the dataset. The result is a dataset with 8 principal component values for each institution.

```{r factor analysis}

library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)


test <- analytic %>% 
  select(inst_type, awardlev, system,
    msi, religious, special_focus, 
    housing, rurality, evening) 

test[] <- lapply(test, as.factor) 

variable_pairs <- expand.grid(Var1 = names(test), Var2 = names(test), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(Var1 < Var2)

# Calculate Cramér's V
results_matrix <- variable_pairs %>%
  mutate(Cramers_V = map2_dbl(Var1, Var2, ~ cramer_v(test[[.x]], test[[.y]]))) |> 
  arrange(Var1, Cramers_V)

print(results_matrix)

corr_test <- analytic |> 
  select(selectivity, online_progs, adult, pell, nonwhite,instruction_exp_fte, tuitionnn,
     num_degrees, i_total_pop) |> 
  cor(, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

print(corr_test)




#Select variables
x <-  analytic |> 
  column_to_rownames(var = "unitid") |> 
  select(inst_type, system, awardlev, special_focus, num_degrees, online_progs, evening, instruction_exp_fte, tuitionnn, msi, adult, pell, nonwhite, i_total_pop, per_undergrad, selectivity) |> 
  na.omit()


#Factor analysis of mixed data
res.famd <- FAMD(x, ncp = 16, graph = FALSE)
summary(res.famd)

eig.val <- get_eigenvalue(res.famd)
print(eig.val)
fviz_eig(res.famd, addlabels = TRUE)
fviz_famd_var(res.famd, repel = TRUE)
fviz_famd_var(res.famd, "quanti.var", repel = TRUE)
fviz_famd_var(res.famd, "quali.var", repel = TRUE)


fviz_screeplot(res.famd, addlabels = TRUE)


#Contribution (%) of each variable to the dimensions
var <- get_famd_var(res.famd)
round(var$contrib[,1:10], 2)




# Table 2. FAMD Dimensions
top_vars <- sapply(1:12, function(i) {
  paste(
    rownames(var$contrib)[order(var$contrib[, i],
                                decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]],
    collapse = ", "
  )
})

table2 <- eig.val[1:12, ] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Dimension") |>
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 2)),
    `Top Contributing Variables` = top_vars
  ) |>
  rename(
    Eigenvalue = eigenvalue,
    `Explained Variance (%)` = variance.percent,
    `Cumulative Variance (%)` = cumulative.variance.percent
  )

print(table2)

write_xlsx(table2, "../data/FAMD_dimensions.xlsx")



#Contribution to Dimensions
    #The red dashed line shows the expected contribution if every variable mattered equally. Variables with bars above the line build the axis
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  1)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  2)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  3)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  4)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  5)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  6)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  7)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  8)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  9)
fviz_contrib(res.famd, "var", axes =  10)


scores <- res.famd$ind$coord
retained_scores <- scores[, 1:10]
summary(retained_scores)

```
 
STEP 2: Use principal components to construct a dissimilarity matrix using the Daisy package and employing an euclidean distance metric. This dissimilarity matrix is then used to conduct a hierarchical agglomerative cluster analysis using a Ward linkage method to identify classes of institutions.

```{r Optimal number of clusters}
# Table 3: Cluster validation
validate_hca <- function(model, distance, level, selected_k) {
  purrr::map_dfr(2:12, function(k) {
    groups <- cutree(model, k = k)
    sil <- cluster::silhouette(groups, distance)

    tibble(
      Level = level,
      k = k,
      Silhouette = round(mean(sil[, "sil_width"]), 3),
      Min_n = min(table(groups)),
      Max_n = max(table(groups)),
      Selected = ifelse(k == selected_k, "Yes", "")
    )
  })
}

)
```

```{r descriptive statistics}
# Descriptive statistics function
desc <- function(df, vars, cats) {
  map_dfr(vars, function(v) {

    if (v %in% cats) {
      tibble(Category = df[[v]]) |>
        filter(!is.na(Category)) |>
        count(Category) |>
        mutate(
          Variable = paste(v, Category, sep = ": "),
          `Mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f", n / sum(n))
        ) |>
        select(Variable, `Mean (SD)`)

    } else {
      tibble(
        Variable = v,
        `Mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)",
          mean(df[[v]], na.rm = TRUE),
          sd(df[[v]], na.rm = TRUE))
      )
    }
  })
}
```

```{r Multinomial logistic regression}

# Predictors
predictors <- c("tot_pop", "pop_density", "perc_ba",
                "med_income", "perc_pov", "perc_unemployed",
                "perc_black", "perc_hisp", "perc_asian")

# Regression data (Cluster 1 = reference)
reg_data <- d6 |>
  select(cbsa_cluster, all_of(predictors)) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    cbsa_cluster = relevel(
      factor(as.character(cbsa_cluster)), ref = "1"),
    across(all_of(predictors), ~as.numeric(scale(.x)))
  )

# Regression
reg_model <- nnet::multinom(
  cbsa_cluster ~ .,
  data = reg_data,
  trace = FALSE,
  Hess = TRUE,
  maxit = 1000
)

if (reg_model$convergence != 0)
  stop("Model did not converge.")

s <- summary(reg_model)
b <- s$coefficients
se <- s$standard.errors

# Variable labels
labels <- c(
  tot_pop = "Total Population",
  pop_density = "Population Density",
  perc_ba = "Bachelor's Degree or Higher",
  med_income = "Median Household Income",
  perc_pov = "Poverty Rate",
  perc_unemployed = "Unemployment Rate",
  perc_black = "Non-Hispanic Black",
  perc_hisp = "Hispanic or Latino",
  perc_asian = "Non-Hispanic Asian",
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept"
)

# Regression results
results <- tibble(
  Cluster = rep(rownames(b), each = ncol(b)),
  Variable = rep(colnames(b), times = nrow(b)),
  B = as.vector(t(b)),
  SE = as.vector(t(se))
) |>
  mutate(
    p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(B / SE)),
    `Est.` = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", B),
      case_when(
        p < .001 ~ "***",
        p < .01  ~ "**",
        p < .05  ~ "*",
        TRUE ~ ""
      )
    ),
    `S.E.` = sprintf("%.3f", SE),
    Variable = factor(Variable,
      levels = c(predictors, "(Intercept)")),
    Cluster = factor(Cluster, levels = as.character(2:8))
  ) |>
  arrange(Variable, Cluster)

# Wide format: Variables as rows, Clusters as columns
column_order <- unlist(lapply(2:8, function(k)
  paste0("Cluster ", k, c(" Est.", " S.E."))
))

table7 <- results |>
  select(Variable, Cluster, `Est.`, `S.E.`) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Cluster,
    values_from = c(`Est.`, `S.E.`),
    names_glue = "Cluster {Cluster} {.value}"
  ) |>
  select(Variable, all_of(column_order)) |>
  mutate(Variable = unname(labels[as.character(Variable)]))

# Full results: OR, CI, and p-values
full_results <- results |>
  transmute(
    Cluster = paste0("Cluster ", Cluster, " vs. Cluster 1"),
    Predictor = unname(labels[as.character(Variable)]),
    B = round(B, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    OR = round(exp(B), 3),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]",
                       exp(B - 1.96 * SE),
                       exp(B + 1.96 * SE)),
    p = if_else(p < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
  )

# Model information
model_info <- tibble(
  N = nrow(reg_data),
  Reference = "Cluster 1",
  AIC = round(AIC(reg_model), 2),
  Converged = reg_model$convergence == 0
)

print(table7, width = Inf)
print(model_info)

# Export
write_xlsx(
  list(
    "Table 7" = table7,
    "Full Results" = full_results,
    "Model Information" = model_info
  ),
  "../data/HCA_multinomial_regression.xlsx"
)


```

```{r map of CBSA Clusters}
# 1. State boundaries: 50 States + DC (exclude Puerto Rico)
us_states <- tigris::states(
  cb = TRUE, year = 2024, resolution = "20m"
) |>
  filter(STUSPS %in% c(state.abb, "DC"))


# 2. CBSA cluster assignments
cluster_key <- cbsa_clusters |>
  transmute(
    GEOID = as.character(cbsa),
    cluster = paste("Cluster", cbsa_cluster)
  ) |>
  distinct(GEOID, .keep_all = TRUE)


# 3. CBSA boundaries and cluster data
cbsa_map <- land_area |>
  sf::st_filter(
    sf::st_transform(us_states, sf::st_crs(land_area))
  ) |>
  mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID)) |>
  left_join(cluster_key, by = "GEOID") |>
  mutate(
    cluster = replace_na(cluster, "Not in sample"),
    cluster = factor(cluster,
      levels = c(paste("Cluster", 1:8), "Not in sample"))
  ) |>
  tigris::shift_geometry()


# 4. Shift Alaska and Hawaii
us_states <- us_states |>
  tigris::shift_geometry()

# Figure 2. CBSA clusters
library(khroma)

cluster_colors <-  c(

  "Cluster 5" = "#88CCEE",

)

map2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = us_states, fill = "white",
          color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = cbsa_map, aes(fill = cluster),
          color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = us_states, fill = NA,
          color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = cluster_colors,
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "CBSA Cluster",
    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  ) +
  coord_sf(datum = NA) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of CBSA Clusters") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )


# Compact combined map using facets

panels <- c("(a) CBSA Boundaries", "(b) CBSA Clusters")

states_both <- bind_rows(
  us_states |> mutate(Panel = panels[1]),
  us_states |> mutate(Panel = panels[2])
)

cbsa_outline <- cbsa_map |>
  mutate(Panel = panels[1])

cbsa_filled <- cbsa_map |>
  mutate(Panel = panels[2])

combined_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = states_both,
          fill = "white", color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = cbsa_outline,
          fill = NA, color = "grey65",
          linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = cbsa_filled,
          aes(fill = cluster),
          color = "white", linewidth = 0.08) +
  geom_sf(data = states_both,
          fill = NA, color = "grey30",
          linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = cluster_colors,
    drop = FALSE,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Panel, nrow = 1) +
  coord_sf(datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +

  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 12, face = "bold",
      margin = margin(b = 6)
    ),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(3, "mm"),

    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "center",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.key.spacing.x = grid::unit(5, "pt"),
    legend.box.spacing = grid::unit(6, "pt"),

    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )


# Remove automatic legend
map_panels <- combined_map +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Custom legend with evenly spaced color boxes
legend_df <- tibble(
  cluster = names(cluster_colors),
  x = c(1, 3.2, 5.4, 7.6, 9.8,
        2.1, 4.3, 6.5, 8.7),
  y = c(rep(1.8, 5), rep(1.2, 4))
)


legend_plot <- ggplot(legend_df) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = x - 0.18, xmax = x + 0.05,
      ymin = y - 0.16, ymax = y + 0.16,
      fill = cluster
    ),
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = x + 0.23, y = y, label = cluster),
    hjust = 0, size = 3.4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = cluster_colors,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0.5, 11.5),
    ylim = c(0.5, 2.5),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(
      fill = "white", color = NA
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )

# Place legend directly below maps
combined_final <- map_panels +
  patchwork::inset_element(
    legend_plot,
    left = 0.13,
    bottom = 0.07,
    right = 0.87,
    top = 0.25,
    align_to = "full",
    on_top = TRUE
  )

print(combined_final)

ggsave(
  "../data/US_CBSA_combined.png",
  combined_final,
  width = 14, height = 5.8,
  dpi = 300, bg = "white"
)
```
